note: Ground truth, written by reading step.html and step-mega.js — NOT by running
the tool and blessing what it found. That distinction is the whole value of
this file: a corpus built from the tool's own output can only ever score 100%.
Several components are BUILT BY JAVASCRIPT after load (mega-nav's items, the
hero slides, the deal tabs, the FAQ accordion). Their selectors are taken from
the template literals in step-mega.js, so the labels describe the page as a
user meets it rather than as it is served.
`hidden: true` marks a component that exists only while opened. The survey
cannot see it, and a scorer that counts it as a miss is measuring the wrong
thing — it is scored separately, under `openable`.

components.why: Seven top-level triggers, each opening a panel of links. One menu, not seven.
role=tablist with five buttons and five sibling panels outside it.
role=tablist. Six buttons over ONE re-rendered region, not six panels.
The same tab-bar shape again, over the accordion below it.
aria-roledescription=carousel, prev/next, dots, and a 6.5s auto-advance.
Five of them, one per finder panel. A selector that matches all five is correct here.
A real <table> with a sticky thead.
role=dialog aria-modal=true, opened from the Search button.
A drawer is a modal by behaviour: it covers the page and traps focus.

A trail: links with a separator between each pair, in text smaller than the body. Labelled `menu` until the rule was decided — it is navigation, but it is not a menu, and it now has a type of its own.

note: The four `.rail` strips are horizontal scrollers with prev/next buttons.
Whether they are 'a carousel' is a judgement call a specialist makes, so they
are held apart from the scored set rather than counted as a miss either way.
